overallAssessment.verdict: data/regions/brecon-beacons.ts is a richly structured location data file with hero copy, key facts, seasonal guides, insider tips, top experiences, FAQs, hidden gems, and food listings. However it cites 'Perplexity research' as one of its primary sources — AI-generated content — which violates the site's no-AI-content policy and means many specific claims (pricing, tourism figures, bus timetables, feeding station times) cannot be considered evidenced until verified against official sources. The markdown file (content/regions/brecon-beacons.md) is a separate, more opinionated draft in a different voice and does not structurally match the TS data. One specific factual error has been identified: the park is described as 'Wales' third-largest national park' when it is in fact the second-largest of Wales' three national parks. The hero image file exists on disk but has no provenance or licence record.
overallAssessment.structuralQuality: HIGH — the TS data file is well-organised with appropriate sections. Suitable as the canonical source once claims are verified.
overallAssessment.factualConfidence: LOW-MEDIUM — fixed geographic/official facts are likely accurate; pricing, tourism figures, transport details, and feeding station times are unverified and may be stale (16+ months old)

criticalIssues.issue: Factual error: park described as 'Wales' third-largest national park'
criticalIssues.diagnosis: Wales has exactly three national parks: Snowdonia/Eryri (~2,130 km²), Brecon Beacons/Bannau Brycheiniog (1,344 km²), and Pembrokeshire Coast (~620 km²). Brecon Beacons is therefore the SECOND largest national park in Wales, not the third. The claim is incorrect as written.
criticalIssues.action: HUMAN REVIEW: confirm the corrected phrasing with the NPA source before publishing. If the intent was 'second-largest in England and Wales' or a UK-wide ranking, that is a different (and possibly correct) claim that also needs sourcing.
